CanEnchantCardType.maps_to: VigorousEnchantment.can_enchant (enchantments.py:448-452) -- `card_type == CardType.ATTACK`, matching Vigorous.cs:13-16. Enchantment.can_enchant (enchantments.py:51-61) + the subclass override. Base CanEnchant (EnchantmentModel.cs:273-294) rejects CardType 4/5/6 (Status/Curse/Quest), then CanEnchantCardType, then an Unplayable card whose pile is PileType.Deck, then a card that already has a (non-stackable) enchantment. The sim folds CanEnchantCardType into each subclass's own can_enchant and replaces the pile-qualified Unplayable test with an unconditional `not card.is_playable` -- equal in practice because every ported grant enchants a DECK card (probe `grants`).

The grant sets amount 8 (events/stone_of_all_time.py:_VIGOROUS_AMOUNT). Additive-only, so BR-1's phase difference cannot bite. AfterCardPlayed.maps_to: VigorousEnchantment.on_card_played (enchantments.py:460-462) -- sets `disabled` for its own card, matching Vigorous.cs:31-38
AfterCardPlayed.issue: Per-replay firing. See guard EG1: C# fires AfterCardPlayed once per Replay iteration (CardModel.cs:1959), so the FIRST play gets the bonus and the second does not; the sim's on_card_played runs once, after the whole loop, so every replay of the same play gets it. EXECUTED (`py tools/audit/enchantment_probes.py replay`): Vigorous(8) on a base-6 Strike played twice by the ported Throwing Axe relic deals 28 in the sim and 20 in the game (6+8 then 6). LIVE: Vigorous comes from the ported Stone of All Time event (events/stone_of_all_time.py:69-71) and Throwing Axe is a ported Ancient relic; an 8-damage error is the largest single-play divergence in this kind.

guards.what: EG1: EnchantmentModel.OnPlay is a DIRECT call inside the per-Replay loop, placed after the card's own OnPlay and before Hook.AfterCardPlayed (CardModel.cs:1904 `for (i < playCount)`, 1931 `await OnPlay(...)`, 1937-1945 `await Enchantment.OnPlay(...)`, 1959 `Hook.AfterCardPlayed`). The sim has no such slot: the three OnPlay ports hang off before_card_played / on_card_played, both of which fire ONCE per card play, outside the replay loop (combat.py:466 and combat.py:514)

guards.what: FOUR-VERB COVERAGE (enchant / upgrade+downgrade / transform / copy) -- stated explicitly so the hole cannot reopen silently. Verb 3, TRANSFORM: CardCmd.Transform (CardCmd.cs:369-451) removes the original from its pile and adds a freshly-built replacement; it never touches Enchantment, and the destroyed original takes its enchantment with it
guards.maps_to: TRANSFORM verdict: FAITHFUL, both engines drop the enchantment. C#: CardCmd.Transform's loop takes `item.GetReplacement(rng)`, calls `item.Original.RemoveFromCurrentPile()` (CardCmd.cs:400) and adds the replacement (CardCmd.cs:437/440); the word Enchantment does not appear anywhere in the method, and neither AfterTransformedFrom nor AfterTransformedTo (CardModel.cs:1625-1631, both empty virtuals -- SovereignBlade is the only override in the source) moves it. So the enchantment dies with the original. SIM: run.transform_card (run.py:406-470) and CardCmd.transform_to_random (cmds.py:415-449) both build the replacement with `make_card(...)`, which carries no enchantment. EXECUTED, this unit: `py -c "import sys,random;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from sts2_rl.run import RunState;from sts2_rl.cards import make_card;from sts2_rl.enchantments import make_enchantment;r=RunState(rng=random.Random(0));c=make_card('strike');r.deck=[c];e=make_enchantment('vigorous');e.amount=2;e.attach(c);n=r.transform_card(c,into=make_card('bash'));print(n.id, n.enchantment)"` -> `bash None`, matching C#. The in-combat twin (CardCmd.transform_to_random on a Sharp'd Strike) also prints a replacement with `enchantment=None`. Same result for all 17 ids. COVERAGE TABLE for this unit -- (1) ENCHANT: the CanEnchantCardType hook entry plus the reachability guard above. (2) UPGRADE / DOWNGRADE: cannot bite here, and that is now executed rather than assumed: `py -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from sts2_rl.enchantments import ALL_ENCHANTMENTS, Enchantment;print(sorted(k for k,v in ALL_ENCHANTMENTS.items() if v.attach is not Enchantment.attach))"` -> `['goopy','souls','steady','tezcataras_ember']`. Only those four override attach() to mutate a static card property (exhausts / retain / cost / eternal), so only those four can be undone by the card rebuild that upgrade()/downgrade() performs. This unit is not one of them -- it works through the modify_* hooks, which are read live off the still-attached enchantment -- so upgrade and downgrade are no-ops for it. (3) TRANSFORM: this entry, faithful. (4) COPY: guard EG2, gap. All four verbs are now on the record; before this pass transform and copy were 0/17.

guards.what: EG2: card COPY drops the enchantment. C# CardModel.CreateClone (CardModel.cs:2168) -> MutableClone -> DeepCloneFields re-attaches the source card's enchantment onto the copy -- CardModel.cs:1204-1209 `(EnchantmentModel)Enchantment.ClonePreservingMutability()`, `Enchantment = null`, `EnchantInternal(clone, clone.Amount)` -- and does the same for the Affliction two lines down (1210-1215). CreateClone itself throws unless the card sits in a COMBAT pile (CardModel.cs:2170-2173), so every copy site is a combat-pile copy. The sim's copy sites rebuild the card from its class and carry only the upgrade level.
guards.issue: MECHANISM EG2, one verdict at every site (rule 3). FIVE ported sim copy sites drop the enchantment, each a `type(card)()` / `make_card(card.id)` rebuild plus a re-upgrade loop with no `card.enchantment` carry: cards/trash_heap_cards.py:18-24 `_clone` (Dual Wield, DualWield.cs:35), powers.py:827-830 (JugglingPower.cs:48), relics/music_box.py:46-48 (MusicBox.cs:78), cards/anger.py:36-38 (Anger.cs:27) and relics/burning_sticks.py:30-32 (BurningSticks.cs:49). All five map to a C# `CreateClone()` call, so all five are the same defect. The sim's OTHER copy paths are correct and are what makes this a bug rather than a design choice: relics/bing_bong.py:37 and events/reflections.py:52 use `copy.deepcopy` (the enchantment rides along), relics/paels_growth.py:39-46 re-attaches Clone by hand, and the per-combat deck copy (run.py:1136 `copy.deepcopy`) carries it too. EXECUTED, this unit: `py -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from sts2_rl.cards import make_card;from sts2_rl.cards.trash_heap_cards import _clone;from sts2_rl.enchantments import make_enchantment;c=make_card('strike');e=make_enchantment('vigorous');e.amount=2;e.attach(c);print(type(c.enchantment).__name__, _clone(c).enchantment)"` -> `VigorousEnchantment None`. The same one-liner run over all 17 ids prints `None` for every one of the 16 that any probe card accepts (souls needs an Exhaust card, so it was run against fiend_fire). RULE 6, both legs -- reachability of the copy site for THIS unit: ATTACK-only (executed matrix A/P/S = True/False/False), so cards/trash_heap_cards.py:18-24 `_clone` (Dual Wield, hand ATTACK|POWER -- trash_heap_cards.py:143-149), powers.py:827-830 (Juggling, every 3rd ATTACK played), relics/music_box.py:46-48 (first ATTACK played each turn) and cards/anger.py:36-38 (Anger copies itself). Every one of the five sites is ported and reachable (Dual Wield from the ported Trash Heap event pool, events/trash_heap.py:17; Anger from the Ironclad common pool; Juggling from cards/juggling.py; Music Box and Burning Sticks are ported relics). LIVENESS: LIVE via Dual Wield (unplayed hand card, Status Normal): the game's copy deals +[amount] on its first play, the sim's does not. Grant path is the ported Stone of All Time event. SECONDARY (false docstring): `_clone`'s docstring claims it "mirrors CreateClone for the sim's needs". It does not -- CreateClone carries the enchantment AND the affliction; `_clone` carries neither. Fifth entry in this stream's false-docstring list.
